newsitem.title: JAPAN: PRESS DIGEST - Top Japan business news - Oct 1.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Top Japan business news - Oct 1.

text.p: Japan's leading international phone company Kokusai Denshin Denwa Co Ltd plans to set up an undersea optical fibre cable network around Japan by the summer of 1999. This move will help speed up cuts in the price of long-distance telephone calls.

Just System Co Ltd and Access Corp have agreed to cooperate in providing services for users linked to the Internet through home electronics such as television sets and word processers, rather than personal computers. Under the agreement, Just System will convert home pages so that they can be viewed using Access's Internet browser. Thirty companies including Matsushita Electric Industrial Co Ltd, Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp, and NEC Corp have also established an organisation for promoting consumer electronics products with Internet capabilities.

Japan Travel Bureau Inc (JTB) plans to boost its recruitment of new graduates, hiring 450 graduates in the next business year starting April 1 compared with an initial plan of 300. JTB employed only 130 new graduates for the business year ending March 31, 1997.

NEC Corp and Packard Bell-NEC Inc of the United States have set up an equally owned personal computer-related joint venture company to produce and sell IBM-compatible personal computers in Japan. The new company, capitalised at 200 million yen, will target sales of 26 billion yen in the business year starting April 1, 1997, and 50 billion yen in the year starting April 1, 1998.

Four Kirin Beverage Corp plants have obtained production licences for low-malt beer. Sapporo Breweries Ltd and Suntory Ltd are currently expanding their sales of the beer. Kirin plans to sell the beer after 1997.
